hairdresser.intro: Learn hairdressing from consultation to finished style. Master braiding, weaving, treatment, and the business of running a salon.

skillDomains.name: Client Consultation
skillDomains.description: Understand what the client wants and what their hair can do.

skills.name: Hair Assessment
skills.description: Read the hair before you touch it.

modules.title: Every head is different
modules.content:
Before any style, assess four things:

  1. Hair type — straight, wavy, curly, kinky; fine, medium, coarse
  2. Scalp condition — dry, oily, irritated, dandruff, flaky
  3. Hair health — damaged, breaking, split ends, brittle
  4. Hair history — relaxed, natural, colour-treated, recently braided

Style choices that work on one head can destroy another. Ask questions before you plan.

modules.title: Running a consultation
modules.content:
Five questions to ask

  1. What style do you want? (Ask for photos)
  2. When do you need it done?
  3. What have you done to your hair in the last 3 months?
  4. Any scalp problems or allergies?
  5. What's your budget?

What to look at

  • Scalp condition
  • Hair density and length
  • Previous damage
  • Hairline and edges

What to say

If a client asks for a style that will damage their hair, say so. Explain the risk. Offer an alternative.

steps.q: A client with thinning edges wants tight braids. What do you do?
o: Refuse and offer a gentler style that protects the edges
steps.f: Tight braids on thinning edges cause permanent hair loss.

steps.q: A client relaxed their hair two weeks ago and wants a colour treatment today. What do you advise?
o: Wait at least 4 weeks — double chemical processing causes severe damage
steps.f: Relaxer plus colour in short succession can break the hair off.

steps.q: A client brings a photo of a style that requires hair twice as long as theirs. What do you do?
o: Explain the difference and offer alternatives

skillDomains.name: Braiding & Weaving
skillDomains.description: The core styling skills that most West African clients want.

skills.name: Box Braids
skills.description: The most requested protective style in West Africa.

modules.title: What makes box braids good
modules.content:
Box braids are the workhorse of the salon. Getting them right requires:

  • Clean sectioning — even squares for even braids
  • Consistent tension — tight enough to hold, loose enough to protect
  • Neat roots — the first inch determines the whole braid
  • Even length — braid to the same point every time

The common mistake

Braiding too tight. Tight braids feel "secure" to a beginner but cause traction alopecia — permanent hair loss along the hairline. Professional braiders prioritise scalp health over tightness.

modules.title: Three-strand technique
modules.content:
The steps

  1. Section hair into a square using a comb
  2. Divide section into three even strands
  3. Begin braiding close to the scalp — first 3 crosses are the tightest
  4. Add extension hair as you move down
  5. Maintain even tension throughout
  6. Finish with a small knot and singe or dip to seal

Speed comes from practice

A beginner takes 8 hours. A professional takes 3-4. The speed comes from muscle memory, not rushing.

steps.q: A client wants medium box braids. How many sections for a full head?
steps.f: Medium box braids typically use 60-80 sections.

steps.q: You notice a client's scalp is red where you've braided. What do you do?
steps.f: Redness means the tension is too high. Loosen immediately.

steps.q: How long should box braids last before removal?

modules.title: Build a braid portfolio
modules.prompt: Photograph 5 different box braid styles you've done (or practiced on mannequins). Include at least: small, medium, jumbo, with colour, and with curls at the ends.
steps: Practice each style on a mannequin or willing friend
Photograph from front, side, and back
Note the number of sections and hours taken
Use it to show prospective clients

skillDomains.name: Hair Treatment
skillDomains.description: Healthy hair is a business. Understand scalp and strand care.

modules.title: Why washing matters
modules.content:
Every service starts with clean hair. Skipping proper washing causes:

  • Product buildup that dulls the hair
  • Scalp irritation
  • Smell
  • Bad braiding results (slippery, uneven)

The process

  1. Detangle dry hair first with a wide-tooth comb
  2. Wet with warm water
  3. Apply shampoo, lather, massage scalp
  4. Rinse thoroughly
  5. Apply conditioner, focus on ends
  6. Rinse with cool water to seal cuticle
  7. Blot with towel — don't rub

modules.title: Scalp conditions
modules.content:
Common conditions

  • Dandruff — white flakes, often dry scalp. Treat with moisturising shampoo.
  • Seborrheic dermatitis — yellowish flakes, greasy, itchy. Needs medicated shampoo.
  • Psoriasis — thick silvery scales. Needs medical treatment.
  • Traction alopecia — hair loss from tight styling. Stop the cause immediately.
  • Fungal infection (ringworm) — circular patches, hair loss. Contagious — refer to a doctor.

The rule

You can treat dandruff. Anything else — refer to a dermatologist. Don't guess.

steps.q: A client has thick, yellowish flakes and an itchy, greasy scalp. What is it?
You notice circular bald patches on a client's scalp with broken hairs. What do you do?
o: Refer to a doctor — could be ringworm or another infection
steps.f: Circular bald patches with broken hairs suggest fungal infection.

steps.q: A client complains of a dry, itchy scalp with small white flakes. Best first response?
o: Moisturising shampoo and scalp oil, with a follow-up in 2 weeks
Hot oil treatment at high heat
steps.f: Dry scalp responds to moisture. Try gentle treatment first.

skillDomains.name: Salon Hygiene
skillDomains.description: Clean tools protect clients and your reputation.

skills.name: Tool Sanitation
skills.description: What must be cleaned between every client.

modules.title: Blood-borne infections spread through tools
modules.content:
Combs, clippers, scissors, and razors can transfer:

  • HIV (rare but possible with contaminated blood)
  • Hepatitis B and C (much more contagious)
  • Fungal infections (ringworm)
  • Bacterial infections (staph)

What must be sanitised between every client

  • Combs — wash and disinfect
  • Brushes — remove hair, wash, disinfect
  • Scissors — wipe with alcohol between clients, deep clean daily
  • Clippers — brush off hair, oil, spray with disinfectant
  • Razors — single use, dispose properly
  • Capes and towels — wash between every client

This is not optional. It is basic professional practice.

steps.q: You just finished a client. Do you need to clean the comb before the next?
steps.f: Always. Between every client. No exceptions.

steps.q: Which is the most effective way to disinfect scissors?
o: Wipe with 70% isopropyl alcohol and let air dry

steps.q: A client nicks their ear during a cut and it bleeds slightly. What do you do?
o: Stop, clean the cut with antiseptic, apply pressure, replace blade, disinfect everything

skillDomains.name: Salon Business
skillDomains.description: Skill pays the bills only if you run the business properly.

skills.name: Pricing & Clients
skills.description: Charge fairly and keep clients coming back.

modules.title: Price for the value you deliver
modules.content:
Under-pricing is the #1 cause of hairdresser burnout.

The four-part price

  1. Materials — braiding hair, shampoo, treatment products
  2. Labour — hours × your hourly rate
  3. Overhead — rent, electricity, tools
  4. Margin — 30-50% for the business to survive

Example

Medium box braids: 5 hours work, braiding hair costs 15,000 Le, overhead is 2,000 Le, your rate is 5,000 Le/hour. Base cost = 15,000 + 25,000 + 2,000 = 42,000 Le. With 40% margin = 58,800 Le.

If you're charging 25,000 Le for the same braids, you're working for under 2,000 Le/hour.

modules.title: Price a full service
modules.prompt: A client wants: wash and condition, deep treatment, medium box braids, and styling. Materials: shampoo and conditioner 5,000 Le, treatment 8,000 Le, braiding hair 18,000 Le. Time: 7 hours. Your hourly rate: 4,000 Le. Overhead: 3,000 Le. Target margin: 35%. Calculate the price.
modules.context: Package pricing helps clients commit and improves revenue per visit.

skills.name: Retaining Clients
skills.description: The cheapest new client is the one you already have.

modules.title: Why clients leave
modules.content:
The five reasons clients don't come back

  1. Late or slow service — you took 8 hours when you said 4
  2. Poor result — the style didn't match what they asked for
  3. Bad attitude — you were rude, dismissive, or on your phone
  4. Price surprises — you charged more than you quoted
  5. Pain — the style hurt

How to keep clients

  • Start on time
  • Match what you promised
  • Be present — no phone during service
  • Quote before you start
  • Prioritise comfort

A client who returns 6 times a year for 5 years is worth 30 visits.

Include fields: name, contact, hair type, past services, notes
